uncited: A pre-trained monocular depth estimation model provides initial depth priors.
- **Outputs:** A set of 3D Gaussian primitives (position, covariance, opacity, spherical harmonics coefficients) and a rendered image/depth map.
- **3D Gaussian Primitives:** Standard 3DGS representation.
- Mean position $\mu_i \in \mathbb{R}^3$.
- Covariance matrix $\Sigma_i \in \mathbb{R}^{3 \times 3}$, parameterized by a rotation matrix $R_i$ and a scaling vector $s_i$.
- Spherical Harmonics (SH) coefficients for view-dependent color.
- **Depth Map:** Rendered depth is computed per pixel.
**Softmax-Scaling Depth Rendering:** To reduce misplaced Gaussians caused by alpha-blending depth averaging, replace standard alpha-blending depth with a softmax-scaled depth rendering.
- Let $d_i$ be the depth of the $i$-th Gaussian along the ray.
**Depth Correlation Loss:** Apply a Pearson Correlation Loss between the rendered depth and the monocular depth estimate.
- Compute local and global Pearson correlation coefficients between the rendered depth map and the reference monocular depth map.

**Unseen Viewpoints Regularization (UVR):** To prevent overfitting and reduce high-frequency artifacts in sparse settings, render images from viewpoints away from the training set and apply a consistency loss.

**Score Distillation Sampling (SDS) and Depth Warping:** For regions with insufficient input coverage, leverage SDS and depth warping to reduce geometry collapse and texture noise while preserving fine details.
**Floater Pruning:** Identify and remove low-opacity Gaussians that are misplaced (floaters).
This heuristic cleans the scene, making the image and depth map sharper.
Uses Gaussian unpooling for few-shot reconstruction.
Excels in fine details but fails on background geometry. [Link](6420-fsgs-training-and-densification.md)
Renders coherent backgrounds but may prune foreground objects incorrectly. [Link](7399-dngaussian.md)
Focuses on edge-aware constraints for disparity. [Link](9140-edge-aware-disparity-regularization.md)
- **Time and Memory Complexity:** Standard 3DGS complexity, plus overhead for monocular depth estimation and SDS gradient computation.
Cleaner and more coherent scene structure than DNGaussian.
- **Limitations:** Relies on pre-trained monocular depth and diffusion models, which may introduce biases if the priors are inaccurate.
SparseGS was proposed to tackle sparse-view 3D reconstruction using 3D Gaussian Splatting.
